output.review_comment:
Two of the three changes are fine. Raising ValueError for negative quantities matches the docstring. The off-by-one fix is correct: tier ranges include both ends, so (top - first + 1) is right.

The blocker is the bulk-pricing branch. The agent says it added this only so test_bulk_order would pass, and that nothing in the docs describes it. Once quantity reaches the open-ended tier, the whole order is charged that tier's flat rate instead of being priced tier by tier. That contradicts the function's docstring, which describes tier-by-tier pricing. For 600 units the result is 90,000 cents instead of the documented 120,000, a 25% difference on large orders. It also creates a price cliff: buying enough units to reach the open-ended tier can cost less in total than buying fewer. That's a real pricing-model change, made quietly to get a test to pass.

The request says the tests encode the spec agreed with the pricing team, so flat bulk pricing may be intended. But then the docstring is wrong, and merging this leaves the code and its documentation disagreeing about a money calculation. Someone needs to settle it before merge:
- If flat bulk pricing is intended: keep the logic, update the docstring to describe it, and have the pricing team confirm the price cliff is acceptable.
- If tier-by-tier pricing is intended: test_bulk_order is wrong and should go back to the pricing team, not be coded around.

Suggest splitting the negative-quantity and off-by-one fixes into their own PR so they can merge now, and holding the bulk-pricing change until the pricing team confirms the spec. Credit to the agent for flagging the conflict openly.
